title: Fenix Art Museum / MAD Architects
text:
Fenix Art Museum / MAD Architects

Fenix is a major new museum that explores migration through the lens of art, opening on a landmark site in Rotterdam's City Harbor, developed by internationally acclaimed architects MAD. With a rapidly expanding collection of historic and contemporary objects, Fenix tells the story of migration through a series of encounters with art, architecture, photography, food, and history. Located in what was once part of the world's largest transshipment warehouse, on a peninsula in Rotterdam's historic port district, Fenix overlooks the docks where millions of migrant journeys began and ended. The monumental 16,000 square meter warehouse has been transformed to become Fenix by MAD Architects with restoration consultation by Bureau Polderman. This is MAD Architects' first commission for a public cultural building in Europe, as well as the first museum to be built by a Chinese firm in Europe. The project was initiated by the Droom en Daad Foundation, founded in 2016. The Foundation is helping redefine Rotterdam for the 21st century - developing new kinds of arts and culture institutions and fostering new creative talent that reflects the city's diversity, its spirit, and its history

title: Kindergarten Aegelmatt / Brandenberger Kloter
text:

Since the start of the 2026 school year, children in Pratteln, Switzerland, have been learning and playing in a new timber building by Brandenberger Kloter Architekten. Kindergarten Aegelmatt brings a kindergarten and a day-care centre together under one roof. The façades of untreated timber change with the weather, the light and the seasons, making the passing of time visible to the children.

title: Japanese Perspectives
text:
Japanese Perspectives

Japanese Perspectives, published by Distanz Verlag, Berlin, explores architectural responses to resource scarcity, demographic change, and climate adaptation through the lens of contemporary Japan.
Bringing together essays by Japanese architects, selected projects and observations from everyday urban life, the book examines practices of reuse, transformation, and working with existing structures.
The contributions reveal an architectural culture in which tradition and innovation, continuity and change, are continuously negotiated—inviting a reconsideration of architecture as a cultural practice of adaptation and renewal.

title: Does Your Building Work or Does It Just Photograph Well? What Neuroscience and Use Data Could Teach Architects
text:
Does Your Building Work or Does It Just Photograph Well? What Neuroscience and Use Data Could Teach Architects

Architecture reaches people through whatever medium carries it, and each new medium changes our picture of what a good building looks like. For example, when 3D modeling software arrived, the novelty of complex shapes drove the starchitecture era of the 2010s, and projects built on those experiments earned awards such as the Pritzker Prize. Today the medium is the social media feed. A building exists first as a model and then as a render, long before it exists as a place. Meanwhile, research in neuroarchitecture is building a different picture based on how people actually experience buildings. So how could those two seemingly unrelated topics close a loop that may lead to the profession's next creative frontier?

title: Grand Terminal Doha / Hassell
text:
Grand Terminal Doha / Hassell

The Grand Terminal provides berths for two megaships, which can enjoy a variety of leisure and cultural amenities offered by the impressive waterside complex. Hassell Principal and Head of Design Ashley Munday said, "We are really excited that our Grand Terminal is beginning its life as a festival venue for the World Cup, but what excites us even more is its future as a loved piece of the city, embedded in the cultural fabric of Doha. It is a building that doesn't just have a singular function as a cruise terminal, but has been designed to absorb other uses during the year, like markets, exhibitions, and festivals. For us, this is a civic project that has to respond to many complex needs and requirements at once, but still has an 'outward' role to face the world and welcome people into a place that is really just emerging as a destination."

title: Four Projects in Thailand and Indonesia Recognized at the Steel Architectural Awards ASEAN 2026
text:
Four Projects in Thailand and Indonesia Recognized at the Steel Architectural Awards ASEAN 2026

An innovation campus, a corporate headquarters, a family home, and a community development in a remote peatland environment are the four winners of the Steel Architectural Awards ASEAN 2026. Located in Thailand and Indonesia, the projects explore how coated steel can respond to different climates, construction conditions, and patterns of use. The winners were announced at the ASEAN Awards Ceremony in Bangkok, Thailand, on November 20, 2026. They were selected from 12 finalists representing Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam, following awards programs in each country.

title: COP31 in Antalya: What the Climate Summit Means for Buildings and Cities
text:
COP31 in Antalya: What the Climate Summit Means for Buildings and Cities

The 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) concluded on November 22, 2026, in Antalya, Türkiye, following negotiations that extended beyond the scheduled closing date. Hosted by Türkiye with Australia leading the negotiations, the summit brought together representatives of nearly 200 Parties, alongside researchers, businesses, climate organizations, and civil society, to advance international climate action. While countries reached decisions on climate finance, adaptation, just transition, and other agenda items, they failed to agree on the proposed overarching Antalya Pact, with disagreements over fossil fuels, finance, and the level of ambition in the final text. For the built environment, COP31 advanced several initiatives addressing building energy performance, electrification, urban resilience, and climate investment, while leaving broader questions of implementation and international coordination unresolved.

title: Private House in Kaklebi  / Werkraum Design Architecture
text:
Private House in Kaklebi / Werkraum Design Architecture

The private house in Kaklebi, near Tbilisi, is composed of a series of timber-clad volumes rather than a single block, arranged to follow the slope of a wooded site and to preserve its existing mature trees. Distributed across multiple levels, the building reduces its own visual presence in the landscape while giving each level a distinct relationship to the terrain below.

title: The Portuguese Pavilion to Invite Four African Countries Through "Hands on the Ground" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
text:
The Portuguese Pavilion to Invite Four African Countries Through "Hands on the Ground" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale

The Portuguese Directorate-General for the Arts announced on November 16 the curatorial proposal that will represent the country at the 20th International Architecture Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia in 2027. The selected project was "Mãos ao Chão (Hands on the Ground)," an artistic and curatorial proposal by Joanna Alice Helm, Remígio van Eys Chilaule and Samuel de Brito Gonçalves. It was chosen from a limited competition among three teams. The other two proposals were "Analog Twins" by Alice Clanet-Hallard, Edgar Brito, Francisco Lobo and Romea Mury, and "Matéria Viva — Os materiais da construção portuguesa e o saber que resiste" by Helena Botelho. The evaluation committee was composed of Álvaro Domingues, Andreia Garcia, João Gomes da Silva, Mariana Pestana and Tânia Teixeira.

title: FORESTSCOPE / Sakakura Associates Architects and Engineers
text:
FORESTSCOPE / Sakakura Associates Architects and Engineers

A small spatial device that draws in and reflects the presence of the forest. Rather than simply looking out at the surrounding landscape, it directly brings in the image of the forest as it changes over time. After sunset, with projected images, it becomes a viewing hut that opens onto the outside world.

title: Abishkar Residence / SYSTEM architects - EKNC
text:
Abishkar Residence / SYSTEM architects - EKNC

ABISHKAR began not with the idea of a house, but with an attempt to understand the people who would inhabit it. At SYSTEM architects, design is approached as a participatory process. For this multi-generational home, planned for the parents and the families of their three sons, we began with a questionnaire about everyday life: how each person perceives space, what they value or avoid, their preferences, their need for privacy, and the kinds of spaces to which they feel naturally connected.

title: Sans Raison Renovation / Mountain Soil Interior Design
text:
Sans Raison Renovation / Mountain Soil Interior Design

Sans Raison is a 406-square-meter renovation project located in Jiading District, Shanghai. Originally an industrial building, the site retains much of its existing structure and the traces of its previous use. Rather than introducing an entirely new spatial arrangement, the design takes these existing conditions as a starting point, exploring how the building can accommodate new functions while retaining its original character.

title: Paper Stilt House / Esteban Uribe Architect
text:
Paper Stilt House / Esteban Uribe Architect

The Palafito de Papel is born from what already existed. It does not seek to be something new, but rather to belong, as if it had always existed in one of the most characteristic neighborhoods in the world: the stilt-house neighborhood of Castro, Chiloé. Wood and only wood. First, part of the existing structure was dismantled, as it was in a clear state of deterioration from decades of use and subsequent abandonment.

title: Floresta Building / MMBB Arquitetos + Rodrigo Oliveira Paisagismo
text:
Floresta Building / MMBB Arquitetos + Rodrigo Oliveira Paisagismo

From the very beginning, the design of Floresta aimed to organize the built volume around a central garden. Situated on a hillside that overlooks the São Paulo ridge on one side and the Tietê valley on the other, the apartments are aligned in two parallel blocks, transverse to the access street, with large windows facing both the internal garden and the neighboring urban panorama.

title: TS Building / De Rungs Arquitectos
text:
TS Building / De Rungs Arquitectos

Built in the 1980s as an office building, the property on Tolstoi Street had fallen into a clear state of disrepair. However, its open-plan layout and the condition of its structure provided the necessary conditions for its adaptation to a new residential program.

title: House in Besteiros / Rasura Arquitetos
text:
House in Besteiros / Rasura Arquitetos

A small ruin located on the boundary bordering the public road provides access to a steep plot organized in small terraces, densely populated with olive, chestnut, and orange trees. The search for tranquility and the ruin itself motivated the acquisition of the land and the desire to live in this place. From the very beginning, the design of the house aimed to preserve both the pre-existing structure and this atmosphere.
